items.title: #249: Anthropic Files for IPO, The Self-Driving Company, AI and the Meaning of Work & Microsoft’s 60,000-Employee Buyout Offer
items.summary: Anthropic has filed to go public, and its S-1 lays out a future of "virtual collaborators," $40 trillion in knowledge work, and a valuation that could top Meta's. Paul Roetzer and Mike Kaput break down the filing. They debate whether Fortune 500 companies can really become "self-driving" by 2030, and dig into Google DeepMind's new research on AGI, wages, and the meaning of work. In rapid fire: Gemini 4 Carbon, Genie 4, and GPT-6.1 Terra; earnings from Google, Microsoft, and Amazon; Microsoft's 60,000-employee buyout offer; Amazon's anti-tokenmaxxing memo; and a new wave of AI security incidents. items.title: What It Actually Takes to Trust an AI System Running on Its Own - with Yogesh Bhagat of CVS Health
items.summary: Customer-facing AI agents often stall between pilot and production, held back by governance overhead and run costs that break the business case. In this episode, Yogesh Bhagat, Vice President of Digital and Technology at CVS Health, explains how autonomous agents earn the right to operate without human oversight by proving consistent, measurable behavior. He discusses validating a shared development platform instead of every agent, pairing small language models with larger judge models to control cost and latency, and giving a small group of customers the full AI experience before optimizing for containment. ​ Learn the exact strategies we use to help leading AI brands and startups connect with their ideal enterprise AI buyers, visit: emerj.com/AD1
